label: Vassiliev Invariants
notes: Open the lecture. Vassiliev invariants organize all finite type invariants into a graded hierarchy. The lecture develops the filtration by order, the symbol that records the leading behavior on chord diagrams, and the four-term and framing relations that constrain which symbols can actually occur.

label: The Filtration by Order
notes: Arrange finite type invariants in a nested sequence indexed by order. Order zero invariants are constants, order one adds nothing new for knots, and each higher order strictly enlarges the space. The associated graded pieces measure exactly the new information appearing at each order, the central object of the theory.

label: Chord Diagrams
notes: Encode the top-order behavior of an order n invariant by a chord diagram: a circle with n chords marking where the double points sit along the knot. Only the cyclic pattern of chord endpoints matters. The leading symbol of the invariant is a function on these diagrams, abstracting away all lower-order detail.

label: The Four-Term Relation
notes: Show that not every function on chord diagrams arises from an invariant. Consistency forces the four-term relation, a linear identity among four diagrams differing by moving one chord endpoint past a neighbor. Together with the one-term framing relation it cuts the space of symbols down to the actual weight systems.

label: Weight Systems
notes: Define a weight system as a function on chord diagrams satisfying the four-term and framing relations. The fundamental theorem, proved via the Kontsevich integral, says every weight system is the symbol of some Vassiliev invariant. Thus the graded space of invariants is identified with the combinatorial space of weight systems.

label: Recap
notes: Close the lecture. Vassiliev invariants form a filtered hierarchy whose graded pieces are governed by chord diagrams modulo the four-term and framing relations. Weight systems classify the possible top-order symbols. The next lecture gives the combinatorial description of these invariants in concrete diagrammatic terms.
